name: Reconsolidation and Retrieval-Mediated Learning
short_description: Memory retrieval temporarily destabilizes traces (~5-6 hour window) during which they can be strengthened by effortful retrieval or updated with feedback; mechanism underlying testing effect
higher_order_principle: Memory retrieval temporarily destabilizes the retrieved trace, opening a reconsolidation window (~5-6 hours) during which the trace can be modified: strengthened by effortful retrieval, updated with new information (feedback), or weakened by interference. This is the mechanism underlying the testing effect: retrieval DESTABILIZES → restabilization STRENGTHENS. It also explains why immediate feedback after testing is more effective than delayed feedback — the reconsolidation window is open.

neural_substrate.requirement: retrieval must ACTIVATE the trace (mere re-exposure may not trigger reconsolidation)
neural_substrate.molecular: restabilization requires protein synthesis, like initial consolidation

parameters.requirement: retrieval must activate the trace fully

parameters.mechanism: Effortful retrieval (low RS) produces stronger reconsolidation due to deeper trace reactivation and more extensive PE signaling
parameters.easy_retrieval: minimal destabilization → minimal strengthening → minimal learning
parameters.failed_retrieval: trace not fully activated → but ATTEMPT generates PE that enhances subsequent encoding (pretesting effect)

parameters.immediate_feedback: delivered within window → INTEGRATED into destabilized trace → error corrected at trace level
parameters.delayed_feedback: delivered after window closes → creates SEPARATE trace → both error and correction coexist

parameters.mechanism: Each retrieval creates NEW hippocampal trace with CURRENT context → multiple traces with diverse associations → more retrieval routes → more robust memory
parameters.connects_to_Bjork: Multiple traces = increased Storage Strength. Diverse contexts = increased accessibility across situations.

scope_conditions: Very strong, well-consolidated memories may resist destabilization
Reconsolidation requires trace REACTIVATION, not just cue presentation
The 5-6 hour window is approximate and may vary with trace age and strength
Demonstrated in fear memory and increasingly in declarative memory
moderators: feedback_timing (immediate vs delayed relative to reconsolidation window)
context_diversity (retrievals in different contexts create more retrieval routes)

interactions.nature: Pattern completion (ED2) is the retrieval mechanism that triggers reconsolidation (ED3).
The testing effect (ED3) is one manifestation of the PE encoding principle (ED6).

ecological_testability: MEDIUM — behavioral testing effect robust; reconsolidation-specific predictions (window duration) difficult to test in educational settings; feedback timing effects testable in classrooms.
